We applied template 324324 to target. Result is a tuple of outcomes: appears to give product(s) as precursors? The output: "(('Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)O)cc2)cc1', 'Nc1ccccc1N'),)". So applying retrosynthetic template yields two fragments: a sulfonyl phenyl with a carboxylic acid (instead of amide) and an aniline (Nc1ccccc1N). The original target had C(=O)N attached to phenyl amine. So template likely breaks amide bond, converting to acid and aniline.

Thus first step: target -> precursor1: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)O)cc2)cc1 (call it acid) and precursor2: Nc1ccccc1N (p-phenylenediamine? Actually aniline with extra N? It's an aniline with an extra N? SMILES Nc1ccccc1N is p-phenylenediamine (1,4-diaminobenzene). Good.

Now need to apply next template 1914396 to each precursor? The route must have at least 3 reactions, using templates in order: 324324, then 1914396, then 733. Likely each step applies to one of the fragments to further break down to simple buyable molecules.

We need to construct a tree where root is target molecule, children is reaction node with template 324324, children are two mol nodes (the precursors). Then each of those may undergo further reactions using next templates.

We need to apply template 1914396 to each of those? Or maybe to one of them, then 733 to the resulting fragments.

Let's try applying template 1914396 to the acid fragment: "Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)O)cc2)cc1".
